pnl_definition: Gross trading P&L per entity: dollar investment gains BEFORE management and performance fees, approximated as capital base x gross return, in USD millions, calendar year. Medallion gross return is reported (Zuckerman) for 2015-2018. Other years are backed out of net returns: 2015-2020 at 5% mgmt / 44% perf (gross = net/0.56 + 5); 2021 at 4% / 44% (net/0.56 + 4); 2022+ at 4% / 36-44% perf with a ~40% mid (net/0.60 + 4). RIEF/RIDA/RIDGE gross = net/0.9 + ~1% in gain years and net + ~1% in loss years. This assumes ~1% mgmt / 10% incentive; the ADV brochure ranges are RIEF 0.20-1.50% / 0-10% and RIDA 0.85-1.00% / 10%. Losses are negative. This is fund-level trading P&L, not the management company's fee revenue or profit; Renaissance publishes no accounts.
headcount_definition: Total firm employees as reported in Form ADV Part 1A Item 5.A at each year's annual filing (late March/early April). The count is approximate, rounded to 10, and excludes clerical staff. The same firm-wide band appears in all three entity rows for a given year. Mid = ADV figure; low/high = -5%/+12% to allow for rounding and excluded clerical staff.
fx_note: All figures are natively USD; no FX conversion is required.
methodology: Per-entity P&L is derived as capital base x gross return, where gross returns are reported or backed out of net returns using the fee schedules disclosed in Form ADV brochures. Medallion capital follows press lore (Zuckerman/WSJ/Bloomberg: ~$9.5-12bn). Form ADV feeder/master gross asset values serve as upper-bound cross-checks, since they include undistributed profits and leverage. Outside-fund capital is anchored on II/FT net-AUM figures (start-2020, Sept 2024, Nov 2025, Jan 2026), with other years backed out of master GAVs using leverage ratios calibrated to the start-2020 anchors (RIEF ~1.56x, RIDA ~2.12x, RIDGE ~1.85x). Firm total is the sum of the two entities, with bands summed. Bands follow the project calibration: derived +/-20-40%, wider where the return itself is low-reliability, and pure estimate for Medallion 2026.

caveats: Renaissance is private and publishes no P&L. Every PnL figure is derived as capital x gross return, and the gross returns are themselves partly backed out from fee assumptions.

Medallion capital is the dominant uncertainty. Press lore puts it at ~$10-12bn, but ADV feeder GAVs ($20.5-28.2bn at YE2020-2022) and the YE2025 master GAV ($61.2bn, levered) imply it may have been materially larger after 2020. The high bands reflect this.

Medallion net returns for 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 come only from low-reliability, possibly circular secondary sources (Quartr chart, Portfolio123 forum, blogs). 2020 (+76%) traces to a single investor quoted by II.
Medallion fees changed: the 5% management fee dropped to 4% from 2021, and performance became 36-44% from 2022. Applying 5%/44% to later years would overstate gross returns.
Form ADV regulatory AUM ($65-166bn) and master-fund GAVs are gross and leverage-inflated; 13F holdings ($64-77bn) are long US equities only. Neither is used as capital.
RIDA and RIDGE returns for 2017-2019 (and RIDGE 2022-2023) were not found and are assumed, so the 2017-2019 outside-fund rows are low confidence.
Return figures vary by share class or series and by cut-off (e.g. RIEF 2020: -19.4% vs -19.94% vs -22.62% to Dec 25; RIDA 2024: 15.6% vs 15.22%).
Firm-total bands are simple sums of entity bands and so are wider than a true 90% interval.
Headcount is a point-in-time ADV figure that excludes clerical staff; it is not a year-average.
Do not confuse with Renaissance Capital (IPO ETF), RenaissanceRe, Medallion Financial, or the unrelated IAPD registrant 'Renaissance Technologies AI Supercomputing Hedge Capital Ltd.' (CRD 338503).
